summary: notification-service suffers a repeating ~24h memory-leak cycle: heap climbs linearly from ~48% to ~97% then OOMKills (exit 137) and restarts, resetting memory. This started immediately after deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00), which added an in-memory template cache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment). CPU (~25%), request_rate (~140/s), and latency (~110ms) are all flat, ruling out load growth, capacity saturation, and dependency degradation. The consumer-lag and error-rate spikes are consequences of GC thrash/lost throughput at the end of each leak cycle and coincide with the three OOM restarts (03-21 22:59, 03-22, 03-23 19:59) - they also occurred on 03-21 and 03-22, before today's 18:00 Kafka retention change. The reported Kafka-replay hypothesis is contradicted by timing (leak began two days before maintenance) and by clean Kafka logs. Best-supported root cause: bad_deployment (unbounded template cache in dep-5402) causing resource_exhaustion (heap OOM).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory template cache (dep-5402) leaks heap -> periodic OOMKill; lag spikes are a consequence, not the cause
ranked_hypotheses.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 (dep-5402, 2026-03-21T00:00) introduced a ConcurrentHashMap template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction bound. Entries accumulate continuously under steady ~140 req/s load, leaking old-gen heap linearly (~48% -> ~97% over ~24h). GC thrash and loss of consumer throughput near the end of each cycle cause the observed consumer-lag and error-rate spikes, ending in OOMKilled (exit 137) and restart, which resets memory and restarts the cycle. Three cycles = three OOMs this week.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 adds in-memory template cache with no eviction bound
Cache grows unbounded under steady load -> linear old-gen heap growth from ~48% at 03-21T00:35
Heap nears 100%, GC thrash reduces consumer throughput -> consumer lag + error-rate spikes
Container exceeds memory limit -> OOMKilled (exit 137) restart at 03-21 22:59, 03-22, 03-23 19:59
Restart resets heap; cycle repeats every ~24h

assumptions: The ConcurrentHashMap cache has no size/TTL eviction (deploy summary lists a bounded key but no eviction)
Restart resets heap so each sawtooth cycle is one leak period
No other memory-consuming change was deployed to notification-service in the window

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance / replay causes consumer lag and heap spike
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 2026-03-23T18:00 Kafka retention change (cfg-2410) triggered a replay/consumer backlog that spiked heap in notification-service and caused the OOM.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing contradicts causation: memory was already at ~95% and climbing since 2026-03-21T00:35, two days before the 2026-03-23T18:00 maintenance; identical lag spikes and OOMs occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 before any maintenance. Kafka logs for 03-23 show only a benign TLS-cipher warning with no reassignment/outage (F13).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic growth / capacity saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Growing request load saturated notification-service memory/capacity and caused OOM.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat ~140 req/s (mean 140.17) and CPU flat ~25% across the whole window; memory leaks even at constant load, so no load growth occurred.

ranked_hypotheses.title: email-provider / external dependency degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external email-provider degraded, backing up the consumer and inflating memory.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: email-provider has no telemetry and no error/evidence points to it; latency p99 stayed flat at ~110ms and error rate stayed ~0.2% baseline, inconsistent with an external provider fault.

facts.statement: notification-service deployed v3.8.0 (dep-5402) at 2026-03-21T00:00, adding an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache.
Memory was flat ~48% on 03-20 and then ramped linearly to ~97% over ~24h periods after 2026-03-21T00:00, sawtoothing down on restarts.
Restart count went 0 -> 1 (03-22) -> 2 (03-23) -> 3 (03-23T20:00), matching three OOMKilled events.
Latest OOMKilled was 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z on container notification-service-7d9f (exit code 137).
CPU (~25%), request_rate (~140/s) and latency p99 (~110ms) are flat with no trend, excluding load/capacity/dependency causes.
Large consumer-lag spikes occur only at ~the OOM restart buckets (03-21 22:00, 03-22 20:00-22:00, 03-23 18:00-20:00), returning to ~60 by 03-23T22:00.
The only config change is kafka cfg-2410 (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000) at 2026-03-23T18:00, two days after the leak began.
kafka logs on 03-23 17:00-23:59 show no errors/reassignments, only a benign deprecated-TLS-cipher warning.

timeline.event: Memory flat ~48% all day; restarts=0; no incidents.
dep-5402 v3.8.0 deployed: in-memory template cache added to notification-service.
Memory begins steady linear climb from ~48%.
First OOMKilled (exit 137); consumer-lag spike in 22:00 bucket (avg 2273).
Third OOMKilled (exit 137) on notification-service-7d9f; lag spike in 18:00-20:00 buckets; lag returns to ~60 by 22:00.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or disable the template cache introduced in dep-5402 (feature-flag off / revert to v3.7.x) and confirm memory stops climbing.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak onset exactly coincides with dep-5402 (2026-03-21T00:00); removing the change should halt the ~24h OOM cycle.

recommended_actions.action: Bound the ConcurrentHashMap template cache: add max-size/TTL eviction (e.g. capped size + LRU, or use a bounded Caffeine/Guava cache) instead of an unbounded keyed map.
recommended_actions.rationale: A cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction grows unbounded under steady traffic.

recommended_actions.action: Raise an alert on old-gen heap >90% trending and on notification-service restarts counter to catch leak onset before the 3rd OOM.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak ran ~24h per cycle over three days before being escalated; earlier heap-trend alerting would have flagged it on 03-21.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT attribute this to the 2026-03-23 Kafka retention change; keep the Kafka maintenance out of the remediation path.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak and two prior OOMs predate the maintenance, and Kafka logs are clean; acting on Kafka would not fix the issue.

data_gaps: No heap-dump or cache-size/size-metric was available to directly prove the ConcurrentHashMap template cache is the leaking object (leak attribution is inferred from deploy timing + unbounded keying, not a measured cache size).
email-provider has has_telemetry=false, so external-provider health could not be directly confirmed (though flat latency/error-rate argue against it).
The 03-21T17:00-19:30 window before the first OOM had only 1 WARN log returned in tc-016 due to truncation (truncated:true), so pre-21:37 log detail for 03-21 is partial.

findings.statement: notification-service deployed v3.8.0 (dep-5402) on 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, change summary 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' with changes 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment' and 'render path uses cache'; status live, not rolled back.

Memory usage for notification-service was flat at ~48% throughout 2026-03-20 (e.g. 47.86, 47.92, 48.12, 48.24, 47.89) and then ramped linearly from ~48% to ~97% over each subsequent ~24h period, sawtoothing down only on OOM restarts.
At fine resolution the memory climb begins right after 2026-03-21T00:00: memory is 46.84 at 00:10 and 47.79 at 00:35, then rises steadily 48.93 (01:00), 49.7 (01:25), 50.35 (01:50), 51.83 (02:15).
The restarts counter is 0 through 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-21 up to 16:00, then becomes 1 at 2026-03-22T00:00, 2 at 2026-03-23T00:00, and 3 at 2026-03-23T20:00.

notification-service logs show 3 OOMKilled ERROR events over the window, first_seen 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, each preceded by repeated 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took Nms' warnings and a slow /internal/metrics request.
The latest OOMKilled (exit code 137) for container notification-service-7d9f occurred at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, immediately after heap warnings peaked with 'full GC took 6488ms'.

CPU for notification-service is flat at ~25% across the entire window (min 21.78, max 28.5, mean 25.01), and request_rate is flat at ~140 req/s (min 115.35, max 172.03, mean 140.17) with no upward trend.
Latency p99 is flat at ~110ms across the window (mean 110.02, range 96.63-124.49) with no degradation trend.

Consumer lag is normally ~60 with brief spikes to 80-120; large spikes appear only in the 22:00 bucket on 03-21 (avg 2273.11, max 17161.92), 20:00-22:00 on 03-22 (avg 790.21/1589.77), and 18:00-20:00 on 03-23 (avg 810.33/1542.68), returning to ~60 at 22:00 on 03-23.
The only cross-service config change in the window is cfg-2410 on kafka: log.retention.ms reduced 604800000 -> 259200000 ('reduce retention to 3 days') at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z.
notification-service consumes from kafka (queue-consume) and calls external email-provider (has_telemetry: false); no upstream callers listed.
Error rate is normally ~0.2% and only flickers to ~13-14% max briefly in the same buckets as the lag spikes (03-21T20:00, 03-22T20:00, 03-23T16:00 and 20:00).
kafka logs in 03-23T17:00-23:59 contain only one WARN ('deprecated TLS cipher offered by client 23ad0a46') and no error, restart, reassignment, or outage events.

refs.quote: deprecated TLS cipher offered by client 23ad0a46

findings.statement: Historical incidents HIST-104 and HIST-112 both attribute lag spikes to Kafka broker maintenance/partition reassignment, but those are past incidents cited as leads, not evidence about this incident.
